assumptions: Family: 2 adults + 2 children (ages 4 and 7) from Conroe, TX; home airport IAH; 5 nights in one hotel room or condo that sleeps 4. Christmas week = Mon Dec 21 to Sat Dec 26, 2026; February week = Mon Feb 22 to Sat Feb 27, 2027 (mom's non-holiday option, the week after the Presidents Day week of Feb 12-21, 2027). White-Christmas probability, snow depth, and temperature values are computed by me from official NOAA GHCN-Daily COOP/SNOTEL station records (1995-2024, Dec 25 snow depth >= 1 inch; late Dec = Dec 18-27 for temperatures and Dec 21-26 for snow depth; mid Feb = Feb 12-21) retrieved through the Regional Climate Center ACIS API (data.rcc-acis.org). Durango snow figures use the SNOTEL station at Purgatory ski-area elevation (8,920 ft) because no long-record snow-depth station exists near the town; Angel Fire uses Eagle Nest (11 mi north, same valley) as its nearest long-record station; Estes Park white-Christmas odds pool the two in-town stations (1993-2024). Drive hours are estimates: open-routing (OSRM) road distance divided by a 65 mph average; add 15-20% for food/fuel stops with kids (the raw engine times run about 15-20% slower than Google Maps). Flight hours are scheduled elapsed times taken from Kayak route pages (nonstop where offered; connecting routes are fastest one-stop estimates). Airfares are Kayak 12-month monthly route averages (December / February) where published, otherwise my estimates inside each route's published typical range; they are typical planning fares, not quotes for these exact weeks. Lodging prices are my estimates for a mid-range hotel room or condo sleeping 4 (the major booking engines block automated reading); treat them as +/-30% planning figures, pre-tax, same property class in both weeks. Canadian prices converted at USD/CAD 1.4257 (Bank of Canada, Nov 13, 2026).

destinations.name: Estes Park (Rocky Mountain National Park)

kid_activities.name: Hidden Valley sledding in Rocky Mountain National Park
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: no minimum; little ones ride with parents
kid_activities.note: $30 is the per-vehicle 1-day park entry fee (NPS); the groomed sledding hill itself is free and is the only designated sledding spot in the park (about 9,240 ft).

kid_activities.name: Winter elk and wildlife watching around town
kid_activities.note: NPS calls winter the best time to view elk, mule deer and coyote in RMNP; large herds graze in and around Estes Park all season.

kid_activities.name: Horse-drawn sleigh ride
kid_activities.note: Local stables run holiday sleigh rides; prices not posted this far ahead - book early for Christmas week (expect roughly $40-60/adult, not verified).

destinations.nature_highlight: Wild elk herds in the snow beneath the peaks of Rocky Mountain National Park, with the park's Hidden Valley sledding hill at 9,240 ft.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Sledding inside a real national park, elk standing at the fence line, and a cozy downtown riverwalk with hot cocoa - big wonder without extreme terrain.
destinations.risks: Altitude 7,700 ft is mild but real for little kids; town snow cover is thinner than the high country (the in-town station's full 1951-2024 record shows many brown Christmases before 2000 - recent-30-year odds are about 89%); US-36 can ice up in storms; Christmas-week lodging books early.

destinations.name: Breckenridge

kid_activities.name: Frisco Adventure Park lift-served snow tubing (20 min north)
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: no published minimum; one rider per tube
kid_activities.note: $55/hour holiday rate (mid-Dec to early Jan); $44/hour regular rate applies Feb 22-27, 2027. Reservations required; sells out on holidays.

kid_activities.name: Two Below Zero dinner sleigh ride (Frisco)
kid_activities.note: Family favorite since 1983 - sleigh ride, hot cocoa, dinner and live music; winter season starts Nov 21; reservations required; seasonal menu/pricing on their site.

kid_activities.name: Children's ski and snowboard school at Breckenridge Resort
kid_activities.note: Peak 9 has one of the biggest beginner complexes in North America; book weeks ahead for Dec 21-26.

destinations.nature_highlight: A snow-globe Victorian mining town set directly under the jagged Tenmile Range, with 15-28 inches of snow normally on the ground in town.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Kids remember the free gondola over the village, tubing down a lit hill at Frisco, and Santa-level magic on Main Street - all walkable.
destinations.risks: Altitude 9,728 ft is the real deal for ages 4-7 (go easy and hydrate the first 48 hours); Christmas week sells out months ahead with common 3-night minimums; I-70 holiday traffic; very high holiday crowds; cold nights around 3F.

destinations.name: Winter Park

kid_activities.name: Wagon and sleigh rides and Barnyard Buddies at Devil's Thumb Ranch
kid_activities.note: A 6,500-acre ranch 15 minutes from Winter Park; sleigh rides meet and feed the horse herd; reservations via the ranch.

kid_activities.name: Children's ski and ride school at Winter Park Resort
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: young-children programs available (confirm ages at booking)
kid_activities.note: Long rated among the best US resorts for beginner and family terrain; holiday lesson slots go fast.

kid_activities.name: Colorado Adventure Park tubing hill (Fraser)
kid_activities.note: Dedicated tubing hill and terrain park 5 minutes from downtown Winter Park; snowmaking underway for the 2026/27 season; book sessions via their site.

destinations.nature_highlight: The Fraser Valley is one of the snowiest accessible valleys in Colorado - 22 inches normally on the ground at Christmas, 36 by mid-February - under the Continental Divide.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: A real horse-drawn sleigh to dinner, barnyard animals to feed, the state's gentlest beginner ski mountain, and snow deep enough to build a fort anywhere.
destinations.risks: Coldest late-December nights of the Colorado options (average low 2F); altitude about 9,100 ft; Berthoud Pass drive from Denver can close in storms; Christmas-week minimum-stay rules and very high crowds.

destinations.name: Durango

kid_activities.name: Cascade Canyon Winter Train (Durango & Silverton)
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: no minimum; child fare is ages 4-11 ($82.08)
kid_activities.note: Coal-fired steam train along the frozen Animas River to Cascade Canyon; Polar Express themed trains also run in December and sell out far in advance.

kid_activities.name: Beginner ski school and kids programs at Purgatory Resort
kid_activities.note: Wide green runs 25 minutes north of town at 8,800 ft; prices and holiday availability at purgatoryresort.com.

kid_activities.name: Soak at Durango Hot Springs
kid_activities.note: Mineral soaking pools just north of downtown; current admission posted at durangohotsprings.com.

destinations.nature_highlight: A coal-fired steam train grinding up the frozen Animas River canyon - the most storybook kid experience in Colorado.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: The train whistle echoing in a snow-covered canyon is the memory kids keep, plus hot springs and gentle beginner slopes.
destinations.risks: Durango town (6,532 ft) is often snow-thin - the 100% white-Christmas figure is from the SNOTEL station at Purgatory ski-area elevation (8,920 ft), 25 minutes north; US-550 mountain passes close in storms; Polar Express trains sell out by summer; no nonstop IAH flights (about 4.8 h via Denver).

destinations.name: Red River

kid_activities.name: Winter tubing at Red River Ski Area
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: must be 42 inches tall (no age minimum)
kid_activities.note: 1-hour evening sessions from 4:30 pm; $30 weekday, $36 weekend/holiday (Dec 26, 2026-Jan 2, 2027 is holiday-priced); often sells out in holiday periods - book online.

kid_activities.name: Torchlight Parade and Fireworks on the ski hill
kid_activities.note: Every Saturday evening in winter - including Dec 26, 2026 and Feb 27, 2027 - skiers descend with flares followed by fireworks over Main Street.

kid_activities.name: Kids ski and snowboard lessons at Red River Ski Area
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: lessons for all ages per the resort
kid_activities.note: Family-owned ski hill at 8,750 ft sitting in the middle of Main Street - kids can walk to lessons from most lodges.

destinations.nature_highlight: A walkable mining-town main street in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains where the ski hill IS the town, elk wander through, and torchlight parades run every Saturday.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Sled, tube, ski, s'mores and the candy shop are all within two blocks - no car needed after you arrive, and fireworks come to you on Saturday night.
destinations.risks: 13-hour drive each way from Conroe; natural snowpack is thinner than Colorado (about 4.5 inches typical town cover - the resort makes snow); US-64 mountain passes; holiday tubing sessions sell out; February flights to ABQ are unusually expensive.

destinations.name: Taos

kid_activities.name: Rio Grande Gorge Bridge walk
kid_activities.note: Walk the rim bridge 650 feet above the Rio Grande, 10 minutes west of town; bighorn sheep are commonly seen; free.

kid_activities.name: Children's ski school at Taos Ski Valley
kid_activities.note: 20 minutes up the canyon at 9,200 ft - the reliable snow is here, not in town; book holiday weeks early.

kid_activities.name: Enchanted Circle snow-play drive
kid_activities.note: 83-mile scenic loop past Eagle Nest Lake and through Angel Fire with free pull-offs for snow play and photos.

destinations.nature_highlight: The Rio Grande Gorge - a 650-foot-deep chasm you can walk across on a bridge, with the snowcapped Sangre de Cristos behind town.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: A bridge over an enormous gorge, a Bavarian-style ski village up the canyon, and the brightest sunny blue-sky days of any snow option.
destinations.risks: Taos town (6,969 ft) has snow on the ground on Christmas only about 1 year in 3 (36%) - snow play is 20 miles away at Taos Ski Valley; mid-February town snow is patchy (0.2 in average); 13.5-hour drive or pricey ABQ flights.

destinations.name: Angel Fire

kid_activities.name: Snow tubing at Angel Fire Resort
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: resort tubing rules apply (small children with an adult)
kid_activities.note: 'As low as $35' booked online regular, $45 on the holiday schedule; sessions 10 am-4 pm (9 am holiday start); one-time $5 access card fee.

kid_activities.name: Kids ski and ride school at Angel Fire Resort
kid_activities.note: Wide, gentle beginner slopes at an 8,600 ft base - among the least intimidating learning mountains anywhere.

kid_activities.name: Sledding on free Moreno Valley hills
kid_activities.note: Open hills along the valley roads with Wheeler Peak (13,167 ft), New Mexico's highest summit, in view; ask lodging hosts for current safe spots.

destinations.nature_highlight: A sunny, wind-protected alpine valley ringed by peaks - Wheeler Peak, New Mexico's highest mountain, stands over the town.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Tubing right at the resort base, bunny slopes with no intimidating crowds, and a village quiet enough that kids hear the sleigh bells.
destinations.risks: Natural valley snow averages only 4-6 inches (resort makes snow); 12.9-hour drive each way; Angel Fire's own weather stations have gaps, so snow stats use Eagle Nest 11 miles north; February ABQ flights are expensive; valley winds can close upper lifts.

destinations.name: Quebec City

kid_activities.name: Village Vacances Valcartier winter playground (tubing, snow rafting, ice slides)
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: height-tiered pricing (about 48 in and under pays less)
kid_activities.note: CAD $39.99+ online for 'tall' guests (about US$28); opens Friday, December 18, 2026; on-site CAD $44.99; snow rafting and 30+ runs - one of the largest winter playgrounds in North America.

kid_activities.name: Dufferin Terrace toboggan run beside Chateau Frontenac
kid_activities.note: Historic wooden toboggan slide over the St. Lawrence, running since 1884; a few dollars per slide, paid on site.

kid_activities.name: German Christmas Market in Old Quebec
kid_activities.note: Free-admission wooden-village market with carousel and treats, late November through about Christmas; confirm the exact 2026 schedule.

destinations.nature_highlight: Montmorency Falls - 83 feet taller than Niagara - freezing into a giant illuminated ice cone, beside a walled 400-year-old city under a foot of snow.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Kids toboggan beside a fairytale castle, tube down a whole winter theme park, sip maple taffy on snow, and see the famous Ice Hotel (tours are also sold at Valcartier; it typically opens in early January).
destinations.risks: Genuinely cold (average late-Dec low 11F, wind off the St. Lawrence); no IAH nonstop - about 5 hours connecting via Chicago/Toronto; very high Christmas-week crowds and the most expensive airfare of the set; French signage; the Quebec Winter Carnival is early February (fun if they pick the Feb 1-6 window instead).

destinations.name: Banff

kid_activities.name: Soak at Banff Upper Hot Springs
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: all ages; youth 3-17 CAD $17.25, under 3 free
kid_activities.note: Adult CAD $19.75 (about US$14); Canada's highest outdoor hot pool under Rundle Mountain; first-come, no reservations.

kid_activities.name: Banff Gondola to the Sulphur Mountain summit boardwalk
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: ages 5 and under ride free anytime
kid_activities.note: Mountaintop Christmas program runs daily Nov 21-Dec 31, 2026; one child free per paying adult in the first two hours each day; adult fares via banffgondola.com.

kid_activities.name: Johnston Canyon icewalk and Lake Minnewanka skating
kid_activities.min_age_or_height: all ages (ice cleats advised for little boots)
kid_activities.note: Frozen waterfalls and a skating lake inside Banff National Park; free access but a Parks Canada daily pass is required per vehicle.

destinations.nature_highlight: Frozen turquoise lakes and elk on Banff Avenue, with a 25-of-25-year measured white-Christmas record in town - the surest snow of any mountain town studied.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Soaking in an outdoor hot pool while snow falls on the peaks, riding a gondola to a boardwalk above the clouds, and skating on a frozen lake inside a national park.
destinations.risks: Parks Canada pass required per vehicle; December nights can drop below -10F; Christmas lodging books out by fall; 1.5-hour airport transfer on Highway 1 in storms; town snowpack is modest (7 in average - the powder is up high); passports required.

destinations.name: Duluth

kid_activities.name: Snow tubing at Spirit Mountain
kid_activities.note: $25 two-hour day session; $29 glow (night) tubing; $20 weekday glow tubing except holiday weeks.

kid_activities.name: Bentleyville Tour of Lights walk-through
kid_activities.note: Millions of lights along the Bayfront - one of the country's largest displays; historically free with donations; confirm the exact 2026 dates (it typically ends just before New Year's).

kid_activities.name: Gooseberry Falls frozen waterfalls on the North Shore
kid_activities.note: Five waterfalls freeze into ice curtains 40 minutes up Lake Superior's shore; a Minnesota state park vehicle permit is required - fee on the DNR park page.

destinations.nature_highlight: Lake Superior's frozen shore - waterfall ice curtains, sea smoke over the lake, and the Aerial Lift Bridge rimmed in ice.
destinations.why_memorable_for_ages_4_to_7: Kids see a Great Lake freeze, tube a lit hill, walk through five million lights at Bentleyville, and watch giant ships under the lift bridge.
destinations.risks: Cold even by trip standards (average late-Dec low 9F, lake-effect snow squalls); lake winds make mid-February bitter; no IAH nonstop (about 5 h via Minneapolis); activities are spread along a 40-minute shore drive.
